newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Santa Isabel plans Ecuador stores.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Santa Isabel plans Ecuador stores.

text.p: Chilean supermarket chain Santa Isabel SA, which already has investments in Peru and Paraguay, is planning to open five stores in Ecuador over the next two years, said finance vice-president Jaime Perry.
"We feel that the Ecuadorean supermarket industry can be improved. We see great potential," Perry told Reuters at a supermarket seminar.
Santa Isabel is in talks to set up the joint venture which will be 60-percent owned by the Chilean firm with the rest owned by a local supplier, he said.
All five stores, which will cost $10 million to build, will be in Guayaquil, Ecuador's largest port.
Santa Isabel, Chile's largest supermarket group, expects sales to climb to $800 million this year from $600 million last year, said Perry.
